assumptions: The selected beachhead consists of first operators retaining primary due-diligence responsibility after simplifications.
Midmarket operators lack satisfactory evidence intake and exception workflows in their existing ERP or trade systems.
Human review can be targeted to exceptions so supplier onboarding does not destroy contribution margins.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: Paid evidence-gap audits with several first operators in one commodity that reveal recurring supplier failures, convert into annual subscriptions, demonstrate acceptable onboarding labor and gross margin, and produce at least one signed broker or ERP-consultant referral channel.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: EUDR makes traceable upstream evidence a gating input to market placement, and coordinating, validating, versioning, and transmitting fragmented supplier evidence addresses a broader problem than a static checklist.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: Operators face shipment and compliance exposure and recurring supplier work, providing a credible budget basis, but no importer has validated the proposed spend or quantified current evidence-management losses.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: Upfront onboarding plus recurring supplier-volume subscriptions can provide good cash conversion and retention. Margins may be eroded by supplier chasing, geospatial review, liability, and support, while the 400-customer wealth path is unvalidated.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: A single commodity among CEE first operators is narrow enough to target and potentially meaningful, but simplifications reduce some downstream scope and the reachable Polish/CEE account base is not established.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: A Polish-language managed gateway could own a regional workflow niche, yet global traceability suites, ERP vendors, customs platforms, and consultants can bundle overlapping capabilities.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: A trusted supplier-evidence graph can extend across commodities, countries, adjacent due-diligence regimes, supplier risk, audit support, and procurement intelligence.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: Resolved supplier identities, historical evidence quality, permissions, and workflow integrations could compound, but suppliers and importers own source data and contracts are unsigned and replaceable.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: Managed supplier chase and localized exception handling may outperform generic tools for midmarket importers, but no measured reduction in onboarding time, rejection risk, or compliance cost is supplied.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: The 2026 and 2027 application dates create an immediate readiness window, while recent scope and system updates reward adaptable workflows; further simplification remains a downside.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: Customs brokers, ERP consultants, and commodity accountants are credible trust channels, but none is signed and the founder has no commodity-chain access, making the first accounts relationship-intensive.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: A one-commodity evidence-gap audit is bootstrappable and fits document AI skills, but truthful upstream data, geospatial accuracy, legal updates, security, and professional liability cannot be automated away.

highest_value_structural_change: Narrow to one commodity and secure a channel partnership plus permissioned reusable supplier evidence, turning a managed compliance service into a distribution-backed evidence network.
main_structural_strength: A near-term regulatory gate creates recurring, high-consequence evidence work and the resulting supplier-resolution graph can compound across customers.
primary_score_limiter: Customer access and upstream data cooperation are uncontrolled, while large compliance platforms can bundle the core workflow.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: Regulatory simplifications have reduced obligations and global trade-compliance platforms may capture the remaining operators before a regional gateway establishes distribution.
